rules.rule: Archive-entry to ROM matching, on top of the src/*.rs rule. Check: any matcher pairing an archive entry with a ROM by name alone tells same-name candidates apart by CRC before the pairing drives a destructive action (trash, prune, rewrite); falling back to an arbitrary candidate when none matches by CRC is a finding; a change widening or narrowing what an entry matches names, in the matcher's doc comment, the consumers that inherit it (check-roms, export-roms, rebuild-roms pruning). Also apply the src/*.rs rule: README.md and CHANGELOG.md cover user-visible changes under the version in Cargo.toml.

Wii U, export and purge paths, which delete files and folders. Check: A command that writes into a user-chosen directory must not recursively delete a directory it did not create in this run. Replace-directory semantics must match the bail-or-skip hygiene of copy_file(..., false), and any deletion computed from per-file metadata must fail closed: a parse error in a referencing file keeps the candidates rather than releasing them for deletion. Also apply the src/*.rs rule: oxyRomon subcommand module. Check: every CLI flag, default value, and behaviour the diff introduces or changes is documented in the matching README.md section, including the flag's interaction with existing options; a change to how roms, DATs or CHDs are matched, renamed or deduplicated contradicts the workflow section or the FAQ, so check those too; CHANGELOG.md gets an entry under the version heading that matches Cargo.toml's version for anything user-visible — a new flag, a new default behaviour, a directory the tool now deletes; do not report internal refactors with no user-visible effect. Also check: one boundary label per `?`-chain, since the same `with_context` label applied twice to one chain renders twice; per-system DAT download outcomes (imported, up to date, failed) come from the one collector in download_dats.rs, and a GraphQL mutation in mutation.rs that loops over systems itself instead is a finding. When the diff removes a dependency, comments naming it are part of the diff: report any comment whose stated premise the diff invalidates.

wux-rs key loading, which dispatches on file format. Check: a loader that dispatches on a parse failure (invalid UTF-8 means binary) positively identifies the binary format before extracting values, not by size alone; where the format carries no magic, as an otp.bin, it checks every structural constraint the format does have (exact size, programmed key slots) and refuses a file that fails them. The refusal error states every accepted format and its exact size, and a test at the exact size boundary of each binary format asserts that a wrong file of that size is refused or yields nothing. Also apply the crates/wux-rs/src/** rule: wux-rs, which writes NUS folders into a caller's directory. Check: A command that writes into a user-chosen directory must not recursively delete a directory it did not create in this run. Replace-directory semantics must match the bail-or-skip hygiene of copy_file(..., false), and any deletion computed from per-file metadata must fail closed: a parse error in a referencing file keeps the candidates rather than releasing them for deletion. Also apply the crates/*/src/** rule: Format crates parse data stored in files that arrive from downloads. Check: any decompression of stored data is capped to the declared expected size before it expands (a limiting reader), any allocation whose length comes from a file field is bounded by the already-checked file size before allocating, and a length or shape assumption on stored data is a runtime check returning an error, not a debug_assert. A header field identifying a variant the reader does not implement — version byte, slot or flag byte — is rejected with a typed error, never ignored.

Web server write paths, which share a process with the MCP tools. Check: every background action in these files (spawn_cli_action, or any other tokio::spawn doing file or database writes) takes WRITE_LOCK from src/mcp.rs before it acquires its connection, the same lock MCP tools take in run_action; one without it can move the same files as another action at the same time. Short settings writes on the request path stay outside the lock by design, so they answer during a long action, and are not a finding. Also apply the src/*.rs rule: OxyRomon subcommand module. chd-rs codec glue, on top of the Rust rule. Check: a constant assumed length or shape of another component's output that the code strips, skips or seeks past (a container header, a magic, a fixed prefix) is validated with a runtime check returning an error, not a debug_assert: release builds skip the assert and silently misalign every record after it. Also: any arithmetic multiplying a hunk index or hunk count by hunk_bytes or unit_bytes is performed in 64 bits; u32 offset products wrap at 4 GiB and corrupt clone maps past that size, which only DVD-and-larger parents expose. Also apply the crates/*/src/** rule: Format crates parse data stored in files that arrive from downloads. Check: any decompression of stored data is capped to the declared expected size before it expands (a limiting reader), any allocation whose length comes from a file field is bounded by the already-checked file size before allocating, and a length or shape assumption on stored data is a runtime check returning an error, not a debug_assert. A header field identifying a variant the reader does not implement — version byte, slot or flag byte — is rejected with a typed error, never ignored.

MCP tool surface reviewed as the interface the model actually reads. Check: every value list in a tool description or parameter doc comment matches exactly what the validation code and the synthesized clap parser accept, including case; every parameter doc comment states the semantics the handler applies to the value (for example a list value replacing the whole list), not only its type; any boolean whose true value triggers an irreversible action defaults so that omitting it reaches the refusal path; a tool reporting per-system outcomes (imported, up to date, failed) maps the shared collector's result from download_dats.rs rather than looping over systems itself; one boundary label per `?`-chain, since the same `with_context` label applied twice to one chain renders twice.

Leptos web UI. frontend/ is rustfmt-formatted (edition 2024) but CI gates it with clippy only, so formatting drift is invisible to the pipeline. Check: run `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on each changed .rs file and report any hunk that lands inside changed code; drift in untouched code is not a finding.

OxyRomon README reviewed as prose against the code it documents. Check: every flag, default, path, command example and supported-format claim still matches the clap definition and the module that implements it, including code added in this diff; counts and lists it states (supported systems, formats, flags) match what the code accepts; two sections of the document do not contradict each other; the diff does not leave a section describing behaviour the diff removed.

Changelog entry reviewed as prose against the code. Check: a global quantifier ('wherever a command', 'every', 'always', 'no longer') holds for every module defining the feature, not only the ones the diff touches; the entry sits under the version heading matching the nearest Cargo.toml.

Shell scripts reviewed against Cargo.toml. Check: every cargo feature, package name and binary the script names still exists after the diff; a diff that removes a feature updates every script, workflow and Dockerfile that names it.

Generated wiki under openwiki/. Check: every repo:// resource path referenced in .claims exists at head, and every claim about external tools, spawned processes or build files still matches the module that implements it; a diff that deletes a source module or drops the last external tool must trigger a wiki refresh. A claim that a build dependency is gone is checked against Cargo.lock at head too, not only the Dockerfile or manifests: a crate can stay in the graph after the binary it wraps is no longer invoked.

SQLite migration, run at startup by sqlx::migrate!(). Check: a data migration that renames or rewrites rows guards every column it writes against the UNIQUE constraints on it, both column constraints and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statements in other migration files (systems.name, systems.custom_name); an aborted migration is an application that will not open. Before accepting a rename as safe, reproduce its constraint set on a scratch sqlite3. A row whose rename is skipped must not be left half-migrated by a later statement in the same file.

Test DAT fixture. Check: the header <name> is the file name without its date and extension, as in the other fixtures (`Test System (20200721) (MAME).dat` has `<name>Test System (MAME)</name>`), so imported system names stay predictable. A fixture that a test imports into another fixture's system, to update it or to vary it, takes that fixture's header <name> instead (`Test System (20200722) (MAME) (Renamed Game).dat` has `<name>Test System (MAME)</name>`, `Test System (20261025) (CDN Missing H3).dat` has `<name>Test System (CDN)</name>`); report a header <name> that is neither its own file name without date and extension nor another fixture's; every rom's size and hashes match the fixture file the tests feed it, and a rom with a `merge` attribute matches its parent's by CRC.

Rust shared code. Check: when a pub fn, trait method or helper changes semantics, every caller visible in the diff and any caller the diff implies still receives the behaviour it assumes; a fix applied at one call site while a sibling call site performs the same read or write is reported; behaviour moved between layers keeps the error, cancel and shutdown handling the previous layer provided; do not report a change that is provably local to the flow the diff touches. When the diff removes a dependency, comments naming it are part of the diff: report any comment whose stated premise the diff invalidates.
